source_review.notes: Reviewed all ten references. Fixed/scaled-work laws, work/span scheduling, and roofline claims were checked against the Amdahl, Gustafson, Brent, Blumofe-Leiserson, and Williams-Waterman-Patterson papers; current performance practice against official LLNL, SPEC CPU 2017, Google Benchmark, OpenJDK JMH, and pyperf documentation. The five ACM DOI targets resolved to the correct publisher records but denied automated content retrieval, so they support durable theorem/bibliographic attribution only, not inaccessible quotations. All five official practice sources resolved directly.

evidence: Definitions and Notation consistently defines n, P, T_1, T_P, speedup S_P, efficiency E_P, cost C_P, overhead O_P, serial fraction f, work, span, and scaled problem n_P.
Time, reciprocal throughput, processor/resource-time, ratios, and abstract work/span units remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Reviewed domains P>0, P>1 for effective fraction, f in [0,1], fixed/scaled normalization, maxima, limits, and comparable-resource qualifications.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/CONPAR-050/report.json records ideal Amdahl times 100/55/32.5/21.25/15.625, speedups 1/1.818/3.077/4.706/6.4, efficiencies 1/.909/.769/.588/.4, and limit 10.
Exercises independently recompute 80/14=5.714 speedup, .714 efficiency, cost 112, overhead 32, effective fraction .0571; and f=.08 Amdahl 7.273/12.5 versus Gustafson 14.8.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Recomputed every division, fixed-work time, ratio, limit, cost, overhead, and effective-fraction term; printed tables round only display values.

evidence: Normalizing fixed work gives time f+(1-f)/P and Amdahl speedup its reciprocal with limit 1/f for f>0.
Normalizing scaled parallel time gives equivalent serial work f+P(1-f)=P-f(P-1); DAG work and critical path independently imply T_P>=max(T_1/P,T_infinity).
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter does not conflate fixed-work, scaled-work, or scheduler/hardware models and restricts isoefficiency and roofline conclusions to explicit overhead/resource assumptions.

evidence: Reviewed P=1/large P, zero/nonzero serial fraction, short/noisy work, negative and superlinear results, cold/warm state, JIT/GC, frequency/thermal drift, SMT/asymmetric/NUMA/GPU resources, and saturation.

Reviewed different output/accuracy, unfair baselines/boundaries, batching, coordinated omission, rejected work, failures/retries, cloud variance, weak-scaling semantic drift, and safety-critical deadlines.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Boundary analysis spans mathematical limits, correctness, measurement resolution, sampling dependence, hardware regimes, workload semantics, economics, reliability, and deployment.

evidence: Baseline and parallel configurations preserve semantic oracle, accuracy, necessary work, and comparable timing boundary; strong tests fix workload while weak tests follow one declared scale rule.
Environment, resource topology, trial protocol, absolute raw observations, failures, output checks, uncertainty, and excluded work remain attributable.
invariant_checking.notes: Checked invariants across preparation, warm-up, ordering, timing, synchronization, validation, sampling, aggregation, counter collection, analysis, and reporting.

evidence: The executable table exactly instantiates the fixed 10% serial fraction model and verifies decreasing ideal time and nonincreasing efficiency over its worker series.
Work/span lower bounds follow separately from capacity and dependency arguments; effective serial fraction is labeled a summary of all nonideal effects, not source-code proof.
proof_review.notes: Proofs cover scoped formulae only; no formal proof of a benchmark, scheduler, hardware counter attribution, statistical population, production scalability, or deadline is claimed.

evidence: Amdahl, Gustafson, DAG, isoefficiency, and roofline models state their different workloads, normalization, and resource assumptions.
Saturation diagnoses, cache explanations, baseline choices, trial summaries, and heterogeneous comparisons are presented as evidence-dependent analyses.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Exact algebra, abstract bounds, projections, measured claims, causal hypotheses, and human safety review remain distinguishable.

evidence: python3 tools/verify_snippets.py CONPAR-050 passed the deterministic formula table with recorded Python version, exact stdout, empty stderr, and exit code zero.

The chapter requires raw independent trials, environment/input/build manifests, randomized order, correctness checks, absolute times, uncertainty, counters, failures, and controlled variants for benchmark claims.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The arithmetic model is not a hardware experiment and proves no speedup, efficiency, scalability, resource attribution, statistical generalization, economic value, or safety.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed outcomes/boundaries, baselines, speedup/efficiency/cost, Amdahl/Gustafson, work/span, strong/weak/isoefficiency, saturation/roofline, experimental design, service load, superlinearity, heterogeneous/economic scaling, and evidence communication.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed equivalent optimized baselines, kernel/end-to-end decomposition, synchronized completion, topology/affinity/frequency controls, warm/cold protocols, randomized independent trials, raw-data retention, distribution/uncertainty reporting, correctness at every configuration, resource counters, regime annotations, failure/retry costs, and reproducible manifests.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet distinguishes fixed/scaled work and model/measurement; exposition advances from comparison contract to evidence; the Amdahl table is reproducible; ten examples cover distinct diagnostic cases; and five exercises progress from arithmetic to aircraft-safety transfer with complete matching answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external performance-science, statistics, HPC, architecture, economics, aviation, meteorology, regulatory, real-time, operational, or safety review is claimed. The model establishes neither measured hardware speedup nor production scalability, cost, deadline, reliability, or safety.
